register.name: Promoting Sustainable Land Management to Achieve Land Degradation Neutrality
register.detail: GEF Trust Fund grant · UNDP · Concept approved 3 June 2026 · Ministry of Land, Water and Environment · Five years
register.note: USD 30.6 million of co-financing; more than 25,000 people, nearly half of them women
register.text: A Global Environment Facility grant of USD 8,401,400, with UNDP as agency, to restore 6,294 hectares of degraded land and improve the management of about 11,851 hectares of farmland, grazing land and forest. It finances land-use plans, training in drought-resilient farming, and new livelihoods in crops, livestock and beekeeping, for the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: ASCENT-GREEN: Resilient Energy Access for Inclusive Development (FP291)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · World Bank · Approved 28 March 2026 (B.44) · Funded activity agreement executed 11 May 2026 · GCF $250M of $695M for 21 nations, Eritrea among them
register.note: No share for Eritrea is published; the GCF financing covers all 21 nations
register.text: A regional programme that uses GCF grants and a loan to draw private companies into distributed renewable energy, clean cooking and productive uses of power, through a regional financing facility, risk-sharing and carbon risk facilities, and a COMESA-led platform for policy and technical assistance. Energy is the standard furthest from reach in Eritrea.

register.name: Community Based Marine and Coastal Ecosystem Restoration
register.detail: Least Developed Countries Fund grant · IFAD · Concept approved 19 December 2025 · Ministry of Marine Resources and Ministry of Land, Water and Environment
register.note: USD 22.3 million of co-financing; about 21,320 households
register.text: A grant of USD 8,932,420 from the Least Developed Countries Fund, with IFAD as agency, for community-led restoration of the Red Sea coast, including about 3,500 hectares of degraded mangroves. It builds climate-smart, nutrition-sensitive and fisheries-based livelihoods into national adaptation, for food and livelihood on the coast.

register.name: GPE System Transformation and Girls’ Education Accelerator grant
register.detail: Global Partnership for Education · UNICEF grant agent · 2025 to 2028 · US$428,536 used by 23 November 2026
register.note: One of three active GPE grants to Eritrea
register.text: A Global Partnership for Education grant, with UNICEF as grant agent, that joins system transformation funds with the Girls’ Education Accelerator, from 2025 to 2028. Education is one of the seven standards: 53.4% of young people complete lower secondary school.

register.name: GPE System Transformation grant
register.detail: Global Partnership for Education · UNICEF grant agent · 2024 to 2027 · US$2,531,202 used by 23 November 2026
register.note: The GPE Board approved a system transformation grant of US$11,820,000 on 10 June 2024
register.text: A Global Partnership for Education grant for the Inclusive and Transformative Reform Agenda for Quality Learning for All Girls and Boys in Eritrea, with UNICEF as grant agent, from 2024 to 2027. It finances the reform of the school system for the education standard.

register.name: GPE System Capacity grant
register.detail: Global Partnership for Education · UNICEF grant agent · 2024 to 2027 · US$163,848 used by 23 November 2026
register.note: One of three active GPE grants to Eritrea
register.text: A Global Partnership for Education grant, with UNICEF as grant agent, for the capacity of the education system, from 2024 to 2027. It supports the education standard alongside the two system transformation grants.

register.name: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Adaptation Project
register.detail: African Development Fund Climate Action Window grant · Approved 21 September 2026 · With UNICEF · To December 2030
register.note: 21 new water systems and 38 rehabilitated, in six regions
register.text: Climate-resilient water for rural communities in Debub, Maekel, Anseba, Gash Barka, Northern Red Sea and Southern Red Sea: 21 new complete water systems, 38 non-functioning systems rehabilitated, and water, sanitation and hygiene in ten health centres and twelve schools, with UNICEF, to December 2030. It aims to bring drinking water within about 500 metres of home, where basic drinking water reaches 51.9% of people.

register.name: Eritrea Energy Integrated Project
register.detail: African Development Fund and Transition Support Facility grants · Approved 18 February 2026
register.note: 34 MW of solar mini-grids and 542 km of lines, for around 306,000 people
register.text: Solar mini-grids for Tesseney, Kerkebet and Barentu under Desert to Power: $37.31 million from the African Development Fund and $20.73 million from the Transition Support Facility.

register.name: Desert to Power Eritrea 12 MW Mini-Grid Project
register.detail: Transition Support Facility grant · Agreement signed 10 March 2025 · Tesseney 6 MW, Kerkebet 3 MW, Barentu 3 MW
register.note: More than 235,000 people, over 160 schools and 90 health centres in Gash Barka
register.text: A grant from the Bank Group’s Transition Support Facility for solar mini-grids in three towns of Gash Barka, serving households, small farms, agro-processing zones and water supply systems. It is expected to improve access to energy for more than 235,000 people and to train and equip 25 local companies, for the energy standard, the furthest from reach.

register.name: Sustainable Smallholder Irrigated Agriculture in Arid and Semi-Arid Lands
register.detail: Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) and the Embassy of Italy, with UNDP · Signed 8 October 2025 · Maekel, Anseba and Gash Barka
register.text: A project signed by UNDP Eritrea, the Embassy of Italy and AICS for irrigated farming by smallholders in drought-prone and degraded areas of Maekel, Anseba and Gash Barka. It aims at stronger food security, better livelihoods and adaptation to climate change, for the food and livelihood standards.
